title: Ananta Training & Distillation: RunPod, LoRA/QLoRA, kleine Spezialisten, Vision und 256K auf 16 GiB
purpose: Additive, budget-gated training and distillation on existing ML-Intern infrastructure, yielding auditable tiny local specialists and experimentally validated long-context inference.
goal: Train small specialist models (<500MB router, mostly <2GB models), vision agents, and run 256K context feasibility tests on RTX 5060 Ti 16GB; allow optional pay-per-active-time RunPod for training only.
invariants: Do not duplicate Hub training orchestrator, Specialist Factory, approval, evidence or worker-leasing boundaries.
Do not claim entire 256K context fits 16 GiB without measured end-to-end weights, cache, overhead and quality.
Do not claim every under-2GB multimodal candidate fits until model weight, mmproj, image-token and KV allocation are measured.
RunPod cloud costs include compute, persistent storage, transfer, cold-start and possible idle fees; no guarantee of same GPU after stop.
Unapproved private data stays local; no background GPU reservation unless explicitly approved.
No automatic training or paid GPU provisioning without explicit per-job approval and a hard budget.

implementation: Extend existing Ananta Hub-owned training, specialist model factory and worker contracts without duplicated orchestration.

success_criteria: RunPod opt-in training cleanly initializes and stops with reproducible actual billed cost, 0 unintended active pods after completed/cancelled job.
At least one sub-500-MB model graduates with evaluated/calibrated improvement or documented no-go.
At least one 500MB-2GB specialist and a vision candidate have reproducible native/converted inference evidence.
16GB 256K benchmark reports actual feasibility and accuracy, not merely config max.
All cloud data and model licenses, provenance, holdout isolation and fail-closed security gates validated.
notes: P0 tasks are a suggested implementation priority, not evidence of implementation.
RunPod pricing/provider details must be dynamically verified at implementation time.
LoRA/QLoRA adapters require compatible HF base; GGUF quantized inference artifacts are not trainable PEFT bases.
